newsitem.title: USA: U.S. bill offered for Hong Kong journalists.
newsitem.headline: U.S. bill offered for Hong Kong journalists.

text.p: A bill to provide 1,500 special U.S. visas for Hong Kong journalists and their families will be introduced when the U.S. Congress reconvenes in January, an aide to a Republican lawmaker said on Monday.

The bill says those eligible for the visas would be Hong Kong or Chinese journalists who have worked in Hong Kong for at least three years and "whose welfare or safety is likely to be subject to threats or harassment due directly to the journalist's work in the news media in Hong Kong."

The bill was drafted by Representative John Porter, an Illinois Republican who is co-chairman of the Congressional Human Rights Caucus. An aide to Porter said the intent of the bill was to protect journalists after China takes over control of Hong Kong from Britain on July 1, 1997.
The legislation would also make spouses and children of these journalists eligible for the U.S. visas. The visas would be valid from 1997 to 2001.
Porter introduced the bill just before Congress adjourned for the year in October but no action was taken. It must be re-introduced when the new Congress meets in January.

In a rare interview with foreign media in June, Lu Ping, the senior Chinese official in charge of Hong Kong affairs, said press freedom would continue in Hong Kong. But he warned that Hong Kong media would not be permitted to advocate independence for either Taiwan or Hong Kong itself.

Up to 3.5 million of Hong Kong's 6.3 million people have travel documents issued by Britain and can travel extensively without visas under existing arrangements. But most of the rest will have to travel with passports of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region of China, as it will be known after the handover.

Britain has agreed to allow visa-free entry for Hong Kong citizens after the handover to China next year, and Hong Kong Gov. Chris Patten has been lobbying other nations to follow suit. European Trade Commissioner Sir Leon Brittan spoke out on Monday in favour of granting Hong Kong citizens visa-free entry to Europe after China takes control.
